response.query: Which specific HTR/ASR and embedding architectures (candidate models), pretraining/fine-tuning strategies, loss functions, and compute estimates should we commit to for pilot and fallback low-resource scripts?
response.answer: For pilot and fallback low-resource scripts, use Wav2Vec 2.0 for embeddings, fine-tune with cross-lingual transfer learning, and employ cross-entropy loss. Compute estimates will depend on model size and available hardware.

results.content: The DGS Corpus is a large collection of recordings of members of the deaf community in Germany communicating in their primary language, German Sign Language (DGS); it was created to be both as a resource for linguistic research and as a record of the life experiences of deaf people in Germany. To assess its usefulness for training and testing ASR systems for Bemba, we explored different approaches; supervised pre-training (training from scratch), cross-lingual transfer learning from a monolingual English pre-trained model using DeepSpeech on the portion of the dataset and fine-tuning large scale self-supervised Wav2Vec2.0 based multilingual pre-trained models on the complete BembaSpeech corpus. We also introduce new annotated datasets useful for future research in Sinhala text classification and publicly release our pre-trained models. **[Pre-training and Evaluating Transformer-based Language Models for Icelandic](/2022.lrec-1.804/)**.
